packet_column_overlay_hint: Point at a field to read what it shows. Drag fields into the tray below to show them as columns in the packet console, in the tray's order - or click a field to add it to the end. Drag or click one in the tray to take it back out.
packet_column_overlay_available_tooltip: Developers: whether students get this field at all.
packet_column_overlay_unavailable: Students aren't given this field, so it isn't offered to them and doesn't show in the packet console.
packet_column_descriptions_time_word: When the packet arrived, in seconds since the capture started. Bursts of packets close together can give away a scan or a flood.
packet_column_descriptions_number: The packet's number in the capture, counting up from 1. Handy for pointing out one packet in particular.
packet_column_descriptions_length: How big the packet is, in bytes. Lots of packets the same unusual size can be a sign of a scan or a flood.
packet_column_descriptions_observer: What saw the packet. For the packet interceptor, it says which side: prerouting is the packet as it arrived, postrouting is the packet as it left, after any changes.
packet_column_descriptions_hack: Which tool caught the packet: arp, sniff, dos, nfq or nmap. Useful when several tools are running at once.
packet_column_descriptions_purpose: Why the tool recorded the packet, in its own words - mostly for packets the game sent itself.
packet_column_descriptions_mac_src: The hardware (MAC) address of the device that sent the packet on this network.
packet_column_descriptions_mac_dst: The hardware (MAC) address the packet was sent to on this network. During ARP spoofing, it shows traffic being sent to the attacker instead.
packet_column_descriptions_ip_src: The IP address the packet came from.
packet_column_descriptions_ip_dst: The IP address the packet is going to.
packet_column_descriptions_direction: Whether this computer sent the packet, received it, or only saw it pass by.
packet_column_descriptions_protocol: The innermost protocol in the packet - the layer that carries what it's really about, like TCP, ARP or a ModBus request.
packet_column_descriptions_layers_word: Every protocol layer in the packet, outermost first - for example Ether/IP/TCP. Shows how each layer is wrapped inside the one before it.
packet_column_descriptions_summary: One plain sentence about what the packet does - who's asking whom for what, or what's being sent.
packet_column_descriptions_mac_word: The sender's and receiver's MAC addresses together, as sender → receiver.
packet_column_descriptions_ip_word: The sender's and receiver's IP addresses together, as sender → receiver.
packet_column_descriptions_variables: For ModBus packets, which registers the packet reads or writes.
packet_column_descriptions_values: For ModBus packets, the register values the packet carries.
packet_column_descriptions_command: For ModBus packets, the full name of the command, like "read holding registers response".
packet_column_descriptions_command_type: For ModBus packets, whether it's a request (asking a device to do something) or a response (the device answering).
packet_column_descriptions_is_modbus: Whether the packet carries ModBus, the protocol the control system's devices talk with.
packet_column_descriptions_is_useful: Whether the ModBus packet changes or reports a register's value - the packets that matter for what the system does.
packet_column_descriptions_is_primary: Whether this is the first request or response of its ModBus exchange, rather than a copy seen again along the way.
packet_column_descriptions_command_word: For ModBus packets, a short name for the command, like "Write Request" or "Read Response".
packet_column_descriptions_modbus_word: For ModBus packets, the registers and their values in one readable column, as registers = values.
packet_column_descriptions_src: Where the packet came from: its IP address, or its hardware (MAC) address if it has no IP address - like Wireshark's Source column.
packet_column_descriptions_dst: Where the packet is going: its IP address, or its hardware (MAC) address if it has no IP address.
packet_column_descriptions_src_host: The sending device's nickname from Configure Hosts, or its address if it has none - so you can tell the PLC from the laptop at a glance.
packet_column_descriptions_dst_host: The receiving device's nickname from Configure Hosts, or its address if it has none.
packet_column_descriptions_src_port: The port the packet left from. Programs pick a port to talk on; the server's side is usually a well-known number like 502 for ModBus.
packet_column_descriptions_dst_port: The port the packet is going to - often says which service it's for, like 502 for ModBus or 443 for secure web.
packet_column_descriptions_service: Which well-known service the conversation is with, worked out from its ports: ModBus, DNS, HTTPS and so on.
packet_column_descriptions_tcp_flags: The TCP flags set on the packet. SYN starts a connection, ACK confirms data arrived, FIN ends a connection and RST cuts it off. A flood of SYNs can be a scan or an attack.
packet_column_descriptions_ttl: Time to live: how many more routers the packet may pass through before it's dropped. Different systems start at different numbers, so it can hint at what sent it.
packet_column_descriptions_payload_lengt: How many bytes of actual data the packet carries, not counting its headers. 0 means it's only managing the connection.
packet_column_descriptions_time_delta: Seconds since the packet before it. Tiny gaps between many packets can mean a flood.
packet_column_descriptions_info: What the packet is, the way Wireshark's Info column says it - short and technical, like "Who has 10.0.0.5? Tell 10.0.0.1" or the TCP ports and flags.
network_action_forms_wifi_device_is_home: matches the home network, so it can't be the Device Name.
network_action_forms_wifi_home_is_device: matches the Device Name, so it can't also be the home network.
form_overlay_hint: Tick the ones to show. Drag them to change their order.
packet_filter_overlay_hint: Point at a section, field or box to read what it matches. Click a box once to show only those packets, again to hide them, and again to stop. Boxes in one field show any of them; different fields must all match. The filter under the boxes is the same thing as text - copy it, paste one in, or type your own.
packet_filter_overlay_text: Filter - copy it, paste one in, or type your own
packet_filter_overlay_custom: This filter does more than the boxes can show, so they're set aside. Edit it here, or clear it to use the boxes again.
packet_filter_overlay_error: Can't read this filter yet: {error} The console keeps the last filter that worked.
packet_filter_describe_combine: Several ticked in one field: any of them is enough. Several hidden: the packet must match none of them. Different fields must all agree.
packet_filter_states_neutral: Not filtering on this. Click to show only these packets.
packet_filter_states_include: Showing only these packets. Click to hide them instead.
packet_filter_states_exclude: Hiding these packets. Click to stop filtering on this.
packet_filter_states_hidden: Developers: students don't get this option. Click to give it back.
packet_filter_tips_dst: Packets going to one of these hosts. Part of an address or nickname is enough.
packet_filter_tips_src: Packets coming from one of these hosts. Part of an address or nickname is enough.
packet_filter_tips_host: Packets to or from one of these hosts.
packet_filter_tips_pair: Packets between two hosts, in either direction - one host on each side of the row. Leave a side empty for that host talking to anyone.
packet_filter_tips_to: Packets sent to everyone on the network (broadcast) or to a group of devices (multicast). Hiding them cuts out a lot of background chatter.
packet_filter_tips_proto: Packets carrying one of these protocols.
packet_filter_tips_icmp: Kinds of ICMP packet - network control messages, like pings.
packet_filter_tips_arp: Kinds of ARP packet - devices asking and telling which hardware address has an IP address.
packet_filter_tips_wifi: Kinds of Wi-Fi frame, from a capture of Wi-Fi traffic itself.
packet_filter_tips_modbus: Packets carrying ModBus, the protocol the control system's devices talk with.
packet_filter_tips_modbus_type: ModBus requests (asking a device) or responses (the device answering).
packet_filter_tips_modbus_command: ModBus reads (asking for values) or writes (setting them).
packet_filter_tips_modbus_full: Both at once: a read request, a read response, a write request or a write response.
packet_filter_tips_modbus_reg: ModBus packets about one of these registers - pick one, or type part of its nickname.
packet_filter_tips_modbus_consequential: Whether the ModBus packet changes or reports a register's value - the packets that matter for what the system does.
packet_filter_tips_modbus_first: Whether it's the first copy of its ModBus exchange, rather than the same one seen again along the way.
packet_filter_tips_observer: Which of the game's tools caught the packet.
packet_filter_tips_dir: Whether this computer sent the packet, received it, or only saw it pass by.
packet_filter_tips_side: For the packet interceptor: the packet as it arrived (before any rewrite) or as it left (after).
packet_filter_about_sections_hosts: Who the packet is between: where it came from and where it's going, by IP address, hardware (MAC) address or nickname.
packet_filter_about_sections_type: What kind of packet it is: the protocols it carries, and for ICMP, ARP and Wi-Fi, what it's doing.
packet_filter_about_sections_modbus: For ModBus, the protocol the control system's devices talk with: whether it's asking or answering, reading or writing, and which registers it's about.
packet_filter_about_sections_meta: How the game itself came by the packet: which tool caught it, which way it was going, and which side of the interceptor saw it.
packet_filter_eval_dst: Checks the packet's destination: its IP address, its hardware (MAC) address, and the nickname Configure Hosts gives that MAC. It matches if any of them contains what you typed, ignoring case - so 10.0.0 matches every 10.0.0.x address.
packet_filter_eval_src: Checks the packet's source: its IP address, its hardware (MAC) address, and the nickname Configure Hosts gives that MAC. It matches if any of them contains what you typed, ignoring case.
packet_filter_eval_host: Checks both ends of the packet, source and destination, the way Source and Destination do - so it matches if either end contains what you typed.
packet_filter_eval_pair: Each row is two hosts. A packet matches if one end matches the first host and the other end the second - whichever way it's going. Each side matches like Source and Destination, by part of an IP, MAC or nickname. An empty side matches anyone.
packet_filter_eval_to: Matches packets sent to the broadcast hardware address (ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff), a multicast one (01:00:5e..., 33:33..., 01:80:c2...), 255.255.255.255, an IP address ending in .255, or a multicast IP (224 to 239.x.x.x, or ff... for IPv6).
packet_filter_eval_proto: Matches if the protocol is anywhere in the packet's layers. HTTP and HTTPS are judged by port (80 or 8080, and 443), since their content is just data to the capture.
packet_filter_eval_icmp: Matches ICMP packets by their type number: ping is an echo request (8), ping reply an echo reply (0), unreachable is 3 and time exceeded is 11.
packet_filter_eval_arp: Matches ARP packets by their operation: a request is 1 ("who has...?"), a reply is 2. Gratuitous means the sender's own IP is also the one asked about - announcing itself, whichever operation.
packet_filter_eval_wifi: Matches 802.11 frames by their subtype. Handshake matches EAPOL key frames - the WPA 4-way handshake.
packet_filter_eval_modbus: Matches packets the game decoded as a ModBus command - reading holding registers or writing a single register. Hidden, it shows everything else.
packet_filter_eval_modbus_type: From the ModBus header: a request is sent to a device, a response comes back from it.
packet_filter_eval_modbus_command: From the ModBus function code: read holding registers (3) or write single register (6).
packet_filter_eval_modbus_full: Type and command together, so one box can pick, say, only the write requests.
packet_filter_eval_modbus_reg: Matches ModBus packets that name the register: exactly, for hreg_4, or by part of its nickname from the register settings. A read response only names its registers once the game has matched it to its request.
packet_filter_eval_modbus_consequential: True for read responses and write requests - the packets carrying values the system acts on. False for read requests and the echoes that confirm a write.
packet_filter_eval_modbus_first: True for the first copy of each ModBus request or response. The sniffer and interceptor can see the same exchange more than once.
packet_filter_eval_observer: Which of the game's tools put the packet in the capture.
packet_filter_eval_dir: From the packet's hardware addresses and the tool that caught it: received means addressed to this computer (or to everyone), sent means from it, passing by means neither.
packet_filter_eval_side: Only packets the interceptor (NFQ Hook) caught have a side. Comparing the two shows exactly what a rewrite changed.
packet_filter_about_to_broadcast: Packets addressed to every device on the network, or to a group of them - ARP questions, device discovery and the like. Hiding them cuts out most background chatter.
packet_filter_about_proto_tcp: TCP: connections that guarantee delivery, in order - web pages, ModBus, remote logins.
packet_filter_about_proto_udp: UDP: single messages with no connection or delivery guarantee - name lookups, time sync, streaming.
packet_filter_about_proto_icmp: ICMP: the network's control messages - pings, and reports that something couldn't be delivered.
packet_filter_about_proto_arp: ARP: devices asking which hardware address has an IP address. Forged ARP replies are how ARP spoofing redirects traffic.
packet_filter_about_proto_dns: DNS: looking up the IP address for a name, like example.com.
packet_filter_about_proto_dhcp: DHCP: a device getting its IP address from the network when it joins.
packet_filter_about_proto_http: HTTP: unencrypted web traffic - anyone capturing it can read it.
packet_filter_about_proto_https: HTTPS: encrypted web traffic. The capture shows who's talking, but not what's said.
packet_filter_about_proto_modbus: ModBus: the industrial protocol the lab's devices use to read and set register values. It has no encryption or authentication.
packet_filter_about_proto_ipv6: IPv6: the newer, longer kind of IP address, like fe80::1.
packet_filter_about_proto_wifi: Wi-Fi frames themselves (802.11) - only in captures from a card in monitor mode.
packet_filter_about_proto_eapol: EAPOL: logging in to a secured network, including the Wi-Fi password handshake.
packet_filter_about_proto_stp: STP: switches telling each other how they're connected, so traffic doesn't loop.
packet_filter_about_proto_lldp: LLDP: devices telling their neighbors what they are and which port they're on.
packet_filter_about_proto_cdp: CDP: Cisco devices telling their neighbors what they are.
packet_filter_about_icmp_ping: A ping: asking another device whether it's there. Ping sweeps find which devices are on a network.
packet_filter_about_icmp_reply: The answer to a ping - the device is there.
packet_filter_about_icmp_unreachable: A report that a packet couldn't be delivered - the device, port or network isn't reachable. Scans of closed ports draw these.
packet_filter_about_icmp_expired: A report that a packet passed through too many routers and was dropped. Traceroute uses these to map a path.
packet_filter_about_arp_request: "Who has this IP address?", asked of everyone on the network.
packet_filter_about_arp_reply: "That IP address is at this hardware address." Replies nobody asked for are a sign of ARP spoofing.
packet_filter_about_arp_gratuitous: A device announcing its own address unasked. Normal when a device joins - and also how an attacker can poison every device at once.
packet_filter_about_wifi_beacon: An access point announcing its network, several times a second.
packet_filter_about_wifi_probe: A device looking for networks, and access points answering.
packet_filter_about_wifi_auth: The first step of joining a Wi-Fi network.
packet_filter_about_wifi_assoc: Asking to join a Wi-Fi network, and the access point's answer.
packet_filter_about_wifi_deauth: Telling a device to disconnect (deauthentication or disassociation). Floods of these knock devices off a network.
packet_filter_about_wifi_handshake: The WPA 4-way handshake that sets up an encrypted Wi-Fi connection. With all four messages, an attacker can try to guess the password offline.
packet_filter_about_modbus_true: Packets carrying a ModBus command the game understands.
packet_filter_about_modbus_type_request: Sent to a device: asking for register values, or telling it to set one.
packet_filter_about_modbus_type_response: Sent back by the device: the values asked for, or confirming a write.
packet_filter_about_modbus_command_read: Reading registers - asking a device for its current values.
packet_filter_about_modbus_command_write: Writing a register - setting a value on the device. This is what an attacker changes to make the system misbehave.
packet_filter_about_modbus_full_read_req: Asking a device for register values.
packet_filter_about_modbus_full_read_res: A device answering with register values - what operators see.
packet_filter_about_modbus_full_write_re: Telling a device to set a register - what the device acts on.
packet_filter_about_modbus_consequential: Packets carrying values that matter: what the device reports, and what it's told to do.
Requests for values and confirmations - they don't carry values the system acts on.
packet_filter_about_modbus_first_true: The first copy of each request or response.
packet_filter_about_modbus_first_false: Repeat copies of an exchange already seen.
packet_filter_about_observer_sniff: Caught by Traffic Sniff, which records what crosses this computer's network card.
packet_filter_about_observer_arp: Sent or caught by ARP Spoof - including the forged ARP replies it sends.
packet_filter_about_observer_dos: Sent by DoS Attack - the flood itself.
packet_filter_about_observer_nfq: Caught by NFQ Hook, the interceptor that can rewrite ModBus values in transit.
packet_filter_about_dir_in: Addressed to this computer, or to everyone.
packet_filter_about_dir_other: Between other devices - this computer only saw it go by. Lots of these during ARP spoofing means it's working.
packet_filter_about_side_before: The packet as the interceptor received it, before any rewrite.
packet_filter_about_side_after: The packet as the interceptor sent it on, after any rewrite.

visual_descriptions_network_mesh: A small internet: routers linked into a backbone, each with its own subnet of hosts, and packets following real hop-by-hop routes between them.
visual_descriptions_telemetry: Scrolling strip charts of control loops chasing setpoints that step every few seconds - overshoot, ringing and settling included.
visual_descriptions_kernel: Packets flowing through a Linux kernel's netfilter hooks - the path iptables rules act on - being filtered, dropped and rewritten along the way.
visual_descriptions_kalman: Vessels on looping courses, each reporting noisy position fixes that a filter turns into a smooth estimated track.
visual_descriptions_wave_grid: A grid of lines whose thickness shows waves rippling out from random points.
visual_descriptions_vector_field: A field of vectors pointing at the mouse, bent and swelled by gusts of wind.
visual_descriptions_constellation: A QAM receiver's constellation diagram: clouds of received symbols scattered around their ideal points.
visual_descriptions_dense_mesh: A much denser network, where traffic shows only as links thickening while packets cross them.
visual_descriptions_proximity: Points drifting across the screen, linked to every neighbor that comes within reach.
visual_descriptions_cycle: Takes turns showing every background, 20 seconds each.
visual_descriptions_none: Just the theme's background color - nothing animated behind the pages.

settings_tooltips_model_colors_fill: HVAC house: the inside of the room, controller, and thermostats.
settings_tooltips_model_colors_text: HVAC house: the thermostat and indicator text.
settings_tooltips_model_colors_coldness: HVAC house: cold air, and the indicator while the heater is off.
settings_tooltips_model_colors_hotness: HVAC house: hot air, and the indicator while the heater is on.
settings_tooltips_strip_chart_sprites: Which parts of the strip charts are drawn. Not used by the game yet.
settings_tooltips_strip_chart_colors: Colors for the strip charts: a theme color name from the list, or any color name or hex code.
settings_tooltips_strip_chart_colors_gri: The numbers, title, and axis labels.
settings_tooltips_strip_chart_colors_pat: One color per plotted line, in order - lines past the last color reuse them from the start.
settings_tooltips_background_visual: Which animation plays in the background.
settings_tooltips_background_detailed: Show the background's extra detail in workspaces too - for the network, its packets. Title and lesson select pages always show it.
settings_tooltips_background_fps: Frames per second for the background animation (1-120). Lower is lighter on slower computers.
theme_editor_gallery_note: Example panels with made-up data, showing the theme as you edit it - hover, click and select to see those colors too.
settings_tooltips_themes: The default themes, then any you've imported. Hover one to see where it came from.
menu_bar_tooltips_settings_button: Open the settings page: general, appearance, graphics, keybinds, troubleshooting and more.
settings_page_notes_theme: Light or dark, and which theme. Changes show at once. To fine-tune colors yourself, see the Theme Editor on the Advanced tab.
settings_page_row_notes_dark_mode: Dark backgrounds with light text, or the other way around. Most themes have both - a few only come in one.
settings_page_row_notes_theme: The default themes, then any you've imported. Light or dark stays as it is.
settings_page_row_notes_theme_editor: Fine-tune every color and surface yourself, with sample panels to try them on.
settings_page_row_notes_import_themes: Opens the imported themes folder. Put theme files (.json) in it and they show up in the Theme list.
settings_page_notes_theme_reset: Put the theme and everything on this page back the way they started.
settings_page_notes_materials: The backgrounds of each kind of widget: its color (click it to pick another) and, if the theme allows transparency, how solid it is - for the mode you're editing (see General).
theme_materials_notes_window: Behind everything: the window and every page's background.
theme_materials_notes_panel: The drawer: each panel's menu bar and the frame around its contents, and the cards on the settings pages.
theme_materials_notes_card: What takes up most of a panel's drawer: cards, consoles, charts, maps, tables and trees.
theme_materials_notes_field: The deepest, in smaller bits: text boxes, the gaps between cards, and scrollbar troughs.
theme_materials_notes_overlay: Dropdown overlays, like the menu bar's groups.
theme_materials_notes_table_header: Column headers of tables and trees.
theme_materials_notes_alternate_row: Every other row of tables and trees - usually like Fields.
theme_materials_notes_selection: Selected items, and selected cells of tables.
theme_materials_notes_row_selection: Selected rows of trees, like the packet console's.
theme_materials_notes_tooltip: The boxes that show on hover.
theme_materials_notes_footer: The bar along the bottom of the window (unless it's set to see-through).
settings_page_notes_ink_materials: The colors of text, outlines and highlights - always solid.
settings_page_notes_data_materials: The colors data is drawn in - status text, models and chart lines - always solid. Each should stand out on Cards, and the chart lines from each other.
theme_materials_notes_menu_bar_text: Titles and labels on panels' menu bars.
theme_materials_notes_field_text: Text in text boxes, consoles and tables.
theme_materials_notes_accent_text: Text on selected rows and the selected tab.
theme_materials_notes_accent: Focus outlines, checked boxes, slider handles and dropdown overlays' outlines.
theme_materials_notes_border: Outlines of text boxes, tables and tabs.
theme_materials_notes_scrollbar_hover: A scrollbar handle under the mouse.
theme_materials_notes_muted_text: Quieter text: column headers, hints, and things that are off.
theme_materials_notes_good: Status that's fine: on, connected, running.
theme_materials_notes_warning: Status worth a look: off, or waiting.
theme_materials_notes_bad: Status that's wrong: errors, or disconnected.
theme_materials_notes_incoming: What comes in: received paths and boats on maps, and the other hosts on the network diagram.
theme_materials_notes_outgoing: What goes out: sent paths and boats on maps, and this computer on the network diagram.
theme_materials_notes_hot: Heat on models: hotness, and the heater.
theme_materials_notes_chart_1: A strip chart line - charts use these in order.
settings_page_notes_background: The animated picture behind the title pages and workspaces. How smoothly it moves is on the Graphics tab.
settings_page_row_notes_visuals_demo: Open the Procedural Visuals page to try each animation and replay its startup. Back returns here.
settings_page_notes_window_effects: How the window opens and closes.
settings_page_notes_appearance_reset: Put everything on this tab back the way it started.
settings_page_row_notes_reset_appearance: The default theme in your system's light or dark mode, every Theme Editor change undone, and the background and window effects back to their defaults.
settings_page_notes_performance_preset: Set the costliest settings at once. Changing any of them afterward makes it Custom.
settings_page_row_notes_performance_pres: Low for slow computers, High for smooth motion. Also sets the background's framerate and animation.
settings_page_performance_preset_notes_l: 5 fps panels, no antialiasing or transitions, still 10 fps background.
settings_page_performance_preset_notes_b: The defaults: 10 fps panels, 30 fps background.
settings_page_performance_preset_notes_h: 30 fps panels and charts, 60 fps background.
settings_page_notes_frame_rate: How often the app redraws - the panels and the background each have their own.
settings_page_row_notes_ui_fps: Updates per second for every chart, map, table and readout (1-60). Higher is smoother but busier; lower is lighter on slower computers.
settings_page_notes_rendering: Drawing quality and animation, the background's too.
settings_page_row_notes_antialiasing: Smooth the edges of lines and text in charts, maps and the background. Off draws faster but jagged.
settings_page_row_notes_page_transitions: Animate changing pages and opening popups. Off switches instantly.
settings_page_row_notes_freeze_backgroun: Hold the background still instead of animating it - lighter on slower computers.
settings_page_row_notes_freeze_workspace: Hold the background still behind workspace panels, where every frame also repaints the panels above.
settings_page_row_notes_disable_workspac: Leave the background out of workspaces altogether.
settings_page_notes_monitoring: See how well the app is keeping up - handy if it feels slow. Measuring only happens while this is on.
settings_page_row_notes_performance_over: Show framerates, frame times, the slowest panels, page load and startup times in the corner. F3 also switches it.
settings_page_row_notes_performance_log: Print the same measurements to the console every few seconds, plus each page's load time.
settings_page_notes_network_helper: Run packet capture in a separate elevated process instead of the main app.
settings_page_row_notes_network_helper: Keeps the main app unprivileged and takes packet decoding off its thread, so heavy traffic lags less. Asks for administrator access when turned on; the main app no longer needs it. Takes full effect on the next workspace you open.
settings_page_notes_performance_reset: Put the graphics settings back the way they started.
settings_page_row_notes_reset_performanc: Every graphics setting back to its default, the background's framerate, motion and detail included.
settings_page_notes_display: How the app's window is shown.
settings_page_row_notes_fullscreen: Fill the whole screen. The Toggle Fullscreen keybind (F11 unless you change it) also switches it.
settings_page_row_notes_fade_in: On startup, the background color fades in, then the window opens, the page comes in, and the background animation starts.
settings_page_row_notes_fade_out: On quit, the window fades away instead of closing at once.
settings_page_notes_keybinds: Keyboard shortcuts that work on every page. Click a box and press the keys to bind them, or clear it to unbind. Keys already bound to another action move to this one. F3 always shows the performance overlay.
settings_page_row_notes_keybind_zoom_in: Make everything bigger by one step. Ctrl = works too while this is Ctrl +.
settings_page_row_notes_keybind_zoom_out: Make everything smaller by one step.
settings_page_row_notes_keybind_zoom_res: Put the zoom back to 100%. Unbound until you set it.
settings_page_row_notes_keybind_fullscre: Switch fullscreen on or off - the same as the Fullscreen checkbox on the General tab.
settings_page_row_notes_keybind_develope: Switch developer mode on or off - the same as the Developer Mode checkbox on the Advanced tab.
settings_page_row_notes_reset_keybinds: Every keybind back to its default.
settings_page_notes_language: The text the app shows comes from a labels file - load another one to change the language or wording.
settings_page_row_notes_labels_file: The labels file in use, on top of the default text.
settings_page_row_notes_load_labels: Pick a labels file to use. Anything it doesn't cover keeps its default text.
settings_page_row_notes_default_labels: Stop using the loaded file and go back to the default text.
settings_page_row_notes_favorite: The workspace the title page's Resume button opens. A workspace's Bookmark button sets this too.
settings_page_notes_access_point: The hardware access point the game connects through.
settings_page_row_notes_ap_config: Open the access point's own configuration page in your web browser.
settings_page_notes_theme_editor: Build your own theme from scratch. Easy to end up with something hard to read - Reset Appearance on the Appearance tab undoes it.
settings_page_notes_saved_data: What workspaces have saved. Asks before deleting anything, and can't be undone.
settings_page_row_notes_delete_workspace: Every workspace's saved entries, toggles and panel sizes go back to their defaults. Your settings here are kept.
settings_page_notes_reset_settings: Something look or act wrong? Put one group of settings back to its defaults - nothing else changes.
settings_page_row_notes_delete_user_data: Everything: workspace data, captures, and every setting on this page. A full reset.
settings_page_notes_diagnostics: Measurements for finding what's slow, printed to the console the app was started from.
settings_page_notes_full_reset: Wipes everything the app has saved, settings included. Asks first, and can't be undone.
settings_page_notes_developer_mode: Tools for building and testing the game itself - for instructors and developers.
settings_page_row_notes_is_developer: Add the debug tools to every page's menu bar, and show the Developer tab.
settings_page_notes_developer_tools: Only shown in developer mode - switch it off on the Advanced tab.
settings_page_row_notes_debug_labels: Show every label's key instead of its text, to find which key a piece of text comes from.
settings_page_row_notes_workspace_editor: Order workspaces, move them between categories, show or hide them on the workspace select page, and create, rename, edit or delete them.
workspace_sorter_intro: Drag a workspace to reorder it, move it to another category, or set it on its own between the categories (like Start Here!), and drag a category by its title - or by its chip in the Categories list on the left - to reorder the categories. Unchecking Shown hides a workspace or a whole category from the workspace select page without losing its place. Sorting changes wait for Save; New Workspace, Rename and Delete happen right away.
workspace_sorter_category_chip_tooltip: Drag to reorder the categories, or click to scroll to this one
workspace_sorter_shown_tooltip: Whether the workspace select page lists this workspace
workspace_sorter_new_workspace_tooltip: Make a new workspace in this category, copying an existing one's layout
workspace_sorter_edit_workspace_tooltip: Open this workspace in the workspace editor
workspace_sorter_open_workspace_tooltip: Open this workspace, as the workspace select page does
workspace_sorter_rename_workspace_toolti: Give this workspace a new name, and its folder a new name to match
workspace_sorter_delete_workspace_toolti: Delete this workspace for good - its folder, labels and every student's saved data for it
workspace_sorter_discard_question: Discard your unsaved changes to the workspace order?
workspace_sorter_numbered_tooltip: Number this category's workspaces on the workspace select page
workspace_sorter_category_shown_tooltip: Whether the workspace select page lists this category
workspace_sorter_remove_category_tooltip: Remove this category - its workspaces move to Not Listed
workspace_sorter_name_needed: Type a name for the new category first.
workspace_sorter_not_listed_note: Not on the list - drag one into a category, or between them, to list it
settings_tooltips_surface_invert_buttons: Give buttons the same text color as everything else, on a background close to the panels, with a clear outline - instead of colored buttons.
settings_tooltips_backgrounds: The picture behind every page. Pick which ones show here on the Procedural Visuals page.
settings_tooltips_background_choices: Which visuals the background pickers list. Turning off the one playing now switches to No Background.
settings_tooltips_strip_chart_auto_fit: Zoom every strip chart to fit its recent data, instead of aligning their time axes.
settings_tooltips_strip_chart_auto_fit_m: How many seconds of history fit mode shows at most.
settings_tooltips_available: What this workspace offers at all. Refresh to apply - panels only check this while building.
settings_tooltips_available_wifi: Network action form: connect to a WiFi network.
settings_tooltips_available_nmap: Network action form: map the devices on the network.
settings_tooltips_available_arp: Network action form: put this computer between two devices.
settings_tooltips_available_dos: Network action form: flood a device with traffic.
settings_tooltips_available_sniff: Network action form: capture packets on the network.
settings_tooltips_available_nfq: Network action form: intercept and rewrite ModBus packets in transit.
settings_tooltips_available_ap_connect: Network action form: connect to the AP.
settings_tooltips_available_encryption: Network action form: switch the AP's encryption on or off.
settings_tooltips_available_ap_tunnel: Network action form: route device traffic only through the AP.
settings_tooltips_available_kalman: Network action form: switch the AP's Kalman filter on or off.
settings_tooltips_available_table: ModBus table form: live register values.
settings_tooltips_available_modify: ModBus table form: rewrite register values in transit.
settings_tooltips_available_mode: Defender ModBus form: the AP's operation mode.
settings_tooltips_register_presets: Picking one resets every register, then sets up the ones it lists.
register_presets_descriptions_default: Puts every register back to its default settings.
register_presets_descriptions_hvac: Shows the HVAC's heater state (HReg 6) and temperature in degrees F (HReg 10), both modifiable.
register_presets_descriptions_submarine: Shows the submarine's speed and rudder (HReg 3-4), X/Y position in meters (HReg 10-11), and bearing in degrees (HReg 12), all modifiable.
footer_tooltips_wifi_disconnected: Not connected to any Wi-Fi network.
footer_tooltips_wifi_restore: Connect to home switches back to:
footer_tooltips_background_off: There's no background. Pick one with Select Background in Quick Settings.
footer_tooltips_background_theme_off: This theme turns the background off behind panels. It still plays on the title menu.
footer_tooltips_background_workspace_off: The background is disabled in workspaces - turn it back on in quick settings or on the settings page's Graphics tab.
footer_tooltips_developer: Developer mode is on ("is_developer" in preferences.json) - debug tools are in every menu bar.
footer_tooltips_debug_labels: Debug labels are on - every label shows its key. Turn them off in Settings.
footer_tooltips_fps: UI frames per second: achieved / target. F3 shows the full performance overlay.
footer_tooltips_session: Time since the app started, at
title_footer_tooltips_issues: Open a GitHub issue for a bug or an idea
menu_bar_tooltips_theme_editor_new: Make a theme of your own, starting from a copy of any theme.
menu_bar_tooltips_theme_editor_make_buil: Save this theme into the app's built-in themes (assets/themes), to ship it.
menu_bar_tooltips_theme_editor_save: Save your changes to this theme's file - a built-in one's in assets/themes. Unsaved themes are marked with * in the list.
menu_bar_tooltips_theme_editor_selector: The theme you're editing: the built-in ones, then your own. Built-in themes can only be looked at (except in developer mode) - make a new theme from one to change it.
theme_editor_replace_built_in: There's already a built-in theme in {name}. Replace it?
theme_editor_made_built_in:
Saved as a built-in theme: {path}

It's in the theme editor now. To offer it in everyone's theme selector, add it to CURATED_THEMES in style.py.
settings_page_notes_theme_general: What this theme is called and what it's like.
theme_editor_row_notes_built_in: Built-in themes can't be changed, except in developer mode. Make a new theme from this one to edit a copy of it.
theme_editor_row_notes_name: What the theme is called in the theme lists.
theme_editor_row_notes_description: What the theme is like, or where it came from - shown when hovering it in the lists.
theme_editor_row_notes_dark_mode: Most themes have a dark and a light mode. Checked, you're editing (and seeing) the dark one; unchecked, the light one. Off for a theme with only one mode (its "modes").
theme_editor_row_notes_transparency: Lets the theme's materials be see-through. Off, the theme is always solid, whatever their opacity.
theme_editor_row_notes_background: Whether workspaces and settings show the animated background in this theme. Off, the window's own color (or gradient) shows behind their panels instead. The title menu always shows it.
theme_editor_row_notes_background_blur: Blurs the background behind see-through panels, like frosted glass. -1 leaves it to each page.
theme_editor_row_notes_panel_radius: How rounded panels' corners are - 0 is square.
theme_editor_row_notes_panel_frame: How thick the frame of Panels material around each panel's contents is. Its scrollbar sits in it.
menu_bar_tooltips_view_button_group: How this page's models and charts look.
menu_bar_tooltips_home_button: Menu (Esc): everything on this bar, spelled out.
menu_bar_tooltips_forward_button: Go forward again, to the page you went back from.
quit_confirm_message:
Are you sure you want to quit?
Anything running will be stopped.
settings_page_notes_buttons: Every button, but the title menu's and the workspace list's. An opacity of 0 leaves out its background or its outline - a ghost button, or just an outline.
settings_page_notes_menu_buttons: The title menu's buttons and the workspace list's. The selected workspace looks hovered.
theme_editor_row_notes_button_radius: How rounded the corners are - 0 is square.
theme_materials_notes_button_hover: The background under the mouse (pressed, a shade darker).
theme_materials_notes_button_border: The line around them - 0% opacity for none.
theme_materials_notes_menu_button_hover: The background under the mouse, and the selected workspace's.
theme_materials_notes_menu_button_border: The line around them - 0% opacity for none.
theme_materials_notes_menu_button_hover_: Their text under the mouse, and the selected workspace's.
